minutes.headline: Water commissioners heard a draft master plan recommending combined PFAS treatment at Lancaster Ave for two wells, plus a separate Keating plant.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners met mainly to hear a consultant present the draft master plan on PFAS treatment, well capacity and water quality. The recommendation is one treatment plant at Lancaster Avenue treating Lancaster and Hickory Hills water, with a separate plant at Keating. Commissioners asked about SRF financing, deadlines, routes and building sizing. No votes were taken other than adjournment.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners heard a consultant present a draft master plan recommending one PFAS treatment plant at Lancaster Ave for the Lancaster and Hickory Hills supplies, plus a separate Keating plant.
No plan was adopted and no votes were taken other than adjournment.
The consultant described a combined plant with a cross-town transmission main and a standalone Keating plant, each with a budget estimate given as a figure in the recording.
The district has applied for state revolving fund financing, which offers zero percent loans and possible principal forgiveness, but first-year funding is capped, so a borrowing vote would be needed.
The consultant advised sending a letter to the SRF program once its project list is final, asking that the changed scope and amount be treated as a carryover project.

why_it_matters: A PFAS treatment plant is a large capital cost for a small water district, and how much of it is covered by zero-percent state loans or forgiveness, rather than borrowed at the bond rate, affects what water customers pay.
Because first-year SRF funding is capped, district voters would likely be asked to approve borrowing for the remainder of the project.
watch_next: The state's final SRF Intended Use Plan, after which the consultant advised sending the carryover letter.
